newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ANGOLA, Feb 27 - Luanda - Due to the change in approval by customs for clearance of cargo, continuous congestion is being experienced in the port area, and discharge of cargo delayed. No berthing delays on product tankers at refinery buoy. Crude oil terminals operating normally.

ISRAEL, March 4 - Haifa - Four vessels due, 1-2 days delay expected. Loading/discharging at berth, 3 general cargo, 2 bulk, 3 containers, 4 tankers, 1 passenger. Waiting at anchorage to load,discharge, 2 general cargo, 2 containers, 2 vessels under repair/drydock, 3 awaiting orders. Ashdod - Two to four days delay expected. Loading/discharging at berth, 11 general cargo, 2 bulk, 3 containers. Waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 8 general cargo, 3 bulk, 2 containers, 1 tanker, 1 vessel awaiting orders. Eilat - One bulker loading/discharging at berth, 2 bulkers waiting at anchorage to load/discharge.

MOZAMBIQUE, March 3 - Nacala - Port working normally (first come, first served basis). No restriction on berthing and sailing at night. Draft restriction 9.5 at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira general cargo berths working normally (first come, first served). Container terminal/other terminals working normally. Pilotage possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 140 metres loa with a maximum draft of 7.5 metres. Two tugs fully operational. Night navigation for larger vessels restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain. Two waverider buoys have been deployed in the approach channel to Beira as part of the CSIR contract with Jica in respect of the study for maintenance and improvement plan of the access channel of the port.

Maputo - Pilotage is now possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 120 metres loa with a maximum draft of 9 metres. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain. All berths working normally and expected to remain so (first come, first served basis). Draft restriction in the channel is 9 metres plus rise of tide of the day.
NAMIBIA, March 3 - Walvis Bay - Working normally.

NIGERIA, Feb 26 - Lagos - Fuel shortage continues, but easing. Port operating normally, no berthing delays reported. Warri - The pipeline from Warri terminal is damaged. Fuel shortage within the country could worsen. Port Harcourt - Operating normally. Unconfirmed reports that the refinery has been operating at reduced capacity in the last week.
